newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco says strike will not affect customers.
newsitem.headline: Inco says strike will not affect customers.

text.p: TORONTO, June 3 (Reuter) Canadian nickel producer Inco Ltd said on Tuesday a strike at its Sudbury, Ontario operation will not affect its commitments to customers.
Striking Sudbury workers walked picket lines in the northern Ontario city on Tuesday after rejecting a contract offer from the company on Monday.

"We have in our supply lines right now between one or two months of supply of product for customers," David Allen, Inco's vice-president of public and government affairs, said in a telephone interview.
"For the short term at least we expect to be selling that to customers and honor our customer commitments and contracts," Allen said.
Inco produces about 430 million pounds of nickel annually and delivers over 500 million pounds of nickel to its customers.
In 1996, Inco bought nearly 100 million pounds of nickel from other sources.
"We would attempt to satisfy our contracts the best way we can which means getting it from another (source)." Allen said.
The Ontario division produces about 230 million pounds of nickel annually. Inco's Manitoba operation and Indonesian division each produce about 100 pounds of nickel annually, Allen said.
Inco's 4,670 unionized Sudbury workers went on strike at midnight on Monday, after voting 60.4 percent against a tentative contract agreement reached last Friday.

The compnay's Port Colborne, Ontario refinery, which processes cobalt, precious metals and electro-nickel, was not affected by the Sudbury strike. Unionized workers at the refinery approved the contract on Monday.
Asked about the strike's impact on Inco's earnings, Allen said: "Clearly there are costs to any shutdown. I don't have any sense at this stage what it would be."
